target_customer: Small and medium businesses needing a phone system
problem: Legacy business phone hardware and software was expensive and lacked advanced features such as transcription, call tracking and CRM integration.
business_model: Subscription at about $30 per month per TechCrunch

founders.name: Anantha Katragadda
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and quoted by TechCrunch on the shutdown.

founders.name: Vamsi Katragadda
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says Profig was founded by brothers Anantha and Vamsi Katragadda. The YC page lists only Anantha.

exit.reason: Co-founder said the product was a pivot from the original idea and they were not passionate enough about it.

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on cloud telephony with transcription and call tracking features; the launch article describes a packaged phone system rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Cloud phone features were copyable and the company had less than three months of market time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action is documented; the company shut down itself within three months of launch.

market_need_then: TechCrunch's August 2012 launch article contrasts Profig with expensive legacy phone systems; no demand metrics were reported.

branding.domain_note: profig.com redirects to a HugeDomains sale page, so the domain is now parked for sale.

brand_strength.rationale: Only two TechCrunch articles exist, the launch and the shutdown, with no sign of brand awareness.

pivots.from: Original idea pitched to YC (not named in sources)
pivots.to: Instant virtual phone system for businesses
pivots.why: Idea developed in office hours with Paul Graham per TechCrunch; the exact date is not given, month approximate to the batch.

outcome_analysis: Profig launched a cloud business phone system in August 2012 after pivoting from its original YC pitch, then shut down by early November 2012. The founder said they were not passionate enough about the pivot, so the cause is founder commitment, which the taxonomy does not cover and is coded as other plus a failed pivot. No funding or traction figures are public.
notes: Pivot date is approximate because the source gives no date. No funding found; the TechCrunch shutdown article gives no amounts. No competitor was named in dated sources and a competitor search returned only current Grasshopper and RingCentral comparison pages, so the list is empty. VCBacked and RoundFunded have profile pages but no figures were visible.
